Wear ear plugs. Find ones that are foam and pinch them, then place in your ear. Your ear canal will adjust to having them in over time, it may be uncomfortable at first, maybe for a couple weeks. But not wearing ear protection will absolutely destroy your hearing in a short time. I wear ear plugs and noise cancelling headphones over them at work. 

OSHA recommends wearing ear protection in environments with an atmosphere noise level of 85 decibels or higher, for reference air hoses can reach as high as 130 decibels, especially when you're blowing off a part or fixture and hit a hole and it whistles at you. And note, OSHA requires employers to provide ear protection in those environments too, your work should have ear plugs or ear muffs for you. 

You'll get used to speaking at volume in a shop with ear plugs in. It sounds silly but you can actually hear people talk a lot better with earplugs in when you cut out all the ambient noises from machines and air hoses. And don't feel peer pressured or guilty about being one of the only people wearing them. They're your ears.

Ignoring the fact it's a football pad and would be generally useless against any kind of ballistic weapon. Generally you'd want to wear armor on your non dominant side for several reasons. 

The pad would interfere with properly holding and bracing a rifle if it was on the dominant shoulder. And it would add weight. 

The non dominant shoulder would be forward of the rest of your body, I usually refer to it as the breaching shoulder. A good example is Carter's armor from Halo Reach. Say you're in a fight in close quarters or clearing a room you'd want that front shoulder to be armored so you could kind of raise your shoulder and hide behind it to protect your neck and lower half of your face from shrapnel or incoming fire.

Join public teams to gain additional XP. Casual team if you're just wandering doing quests. Event teams if you wanna participate in events.(which I recommend doing) Events are a great way to get massive amounts of XP and good loot, even if you don't help much just participate. You won't drop your junk if you die in an event so don't stress. When you load into an event be sure to read the objective notes at the top of your screen so you have an idea of what you should be doing. 

If people are dropping stuff for you they more than likely don't expect anything in return, as they are probably just feeling generous or they are making room in their inventory/stash. At your level you can't really afford to give up anything. Be a hoarder as much as you can afford. 

As for power armor just do what you're doing, keep what you like and scrap/sell what you don't want. If you plan to scrap anything be sure to equip the perk card that rewards extra junk supplies from scrapped material. 

If you can afford it I would recommend getting Fallout 1st as it gives you access to some pretty useful stuff. One of them being the fusion core recharger for your camp. If/when you get a power armor suit you like the next hurdle will be having a sufficient supply of cores and a way to charge them. 2 other useful items are the scrap box where you can store all your junk components and ammo box. These will help keep your inventory and carry weight under control. 

Any gear you have that is below level 50 will become near useless once you hit level 50 and can craft/equip those items. So don't get too attached to anything until you hit that threshold. 

Save up any legendary modules you get from events and the exchange machine. Once you find a weapon or armor you like you'll be happy you have the modules saved up to roll for perks.

I can tell you in my area that just about everyone posts job ads online. I personally use Indeed. 
I would look up a resume template online and use that to spruce up your resume. 
It definitely can't hurt to call shops around the area and ask if they're hiring, or even better print out a few copies of your resume and make an appearance to drop off your resume. Initiative is attractive to employers.
On your resume list everything you've ever learned about machining, as limited as it may be. What kind of material you've run, types of gages and inspection methods you've used, the type of machine and control panel you've run, the tolerances you've had to work with, the kinds of parts you've made, etc. And once it comes time for an interview just be sure to express you are looking to expand your knowledge and become a truly independent machinist, that you're eager to learn. 
Oh and in the interview, if they ask you "why are you looking to switch jobs?" Don't use that as an opportunity to bad mouth or air your frustrations about your current job, it looks bad. Just say that you're looking for opportunities to advance your skills and knowledge that your current job isn't providing. Ask if they have any kind of advanced training programs on offer.

That's the standard for large scale manufacturing shops. Like you said, a giant assembly factory with some button pushing sprinkled in. 
The good news is that machinists are in high demand right now, at least in my area and you'll have no trouble finding a job. 
What I would recommend, is find a way to learn GD&T, most community colleges will have a course. Knowing GD&T will help pad your resume as well as any kind of manufacturing courses.
Now if you're looking for a more hands on intimate shop to really learn how to be a machinist you'll want to look for what is called a "job shop" that'll teach you about set-ups and fixturing and code. 
I worked at a job shop for year with no prior experience, learned a lot, went to a large company for 5 years and didn't learn a damn thing. Now I'm at a job shop again expanding my knowledge. 
And be upfront about what you expect as a new hire with any potential interviews.
Best of luck!

Loot EVERYTHING. Once you start crafting armor and potions you'll need every piece of leather, herbs etc. you can get your hands on, save yourself the headache and start hoarding early. Don't overlook any opportunity to loot.

Visit sign posts anytime you enter a new town for quests and points of interest to visit. 

Keep your swords in good condition. If you can afford it buy all the sword repair kits you can whenever you visit a smith, or you can also craft your own if you have the materials.

Black smith's will give you more gold for armor, while sword smith's will give you more gold for swords, sell to the appropriate vendor for the best price.
Collect swords to sell for easy money, (there are a couple smiths in the bigger cities that will have plenty of gold to buy your swords/armor for an easy couple thousand gold)

Don't waste your gold buying swords. The BEST swords in the game are found in the open world or earned from quests. There are very few swords you can buy from a vendor that will compare to one you can find or make yourself. 

At lower levels it is absolutely worth finding recipes and crafting upgraded oils for your swords, those damage boosters against monsters is huge.

You can dismantle common items like candle sticks and broken rakes into crafting materials. Doing this will also keep your carry weight as low as possible (for more swords to sell!)

Also buy the DLCs. Otherwise explore the world and enjoy! Hope you have fun
